'''Gilbert Jay Arenas Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|r|iː|n|ə|z}} {{respell|ə|REE|nəz}}; born January 6, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Arenas attended [[Grant High School (Los Angeles)|Grant High School]] in the [[Valley Glen, Los Angeles|Valley Glen]] district of [[Los Angeles]], and accepted a scholarship offer to the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|University of Arizona]] late in his junior year. He was drafted by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 31st overall pick in the [[2001 NBA draft]].

Arenas was a three-time [[NBA All-Star]], three-time member of the [[All-NBA Team]] during his time in Washington, and was voted the [[NBA Most Improved Player]] in the [[2002–03 NBA season|2002–03 season]] in his final season in Golden State. Arenas was nicknamed "'''Agent Zero'''" while playing with Washington, due to his jersey number (0).<ref name="McKenna 2010">{{cite web|url=http://www.washingtoncitypaper.com/display.php?id=38336 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120919052034/http://www.washingtoncitypaper.com/display.php?id=38336 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 19, 2012 |title=Arenas: Agent Zero to Agent of Misfortune |last=McKenna |first=Dave |newspaper=[[Washington City Paper]] |date=January 15, 2010 |access-date=September 23, 2010 }}</ref> He was also nicknamed "'''[[Shichirin|Hibachi]]'''" for "cooking" his opponents. This nickname also referred to his ability to "heat up" quickly. Both names quickly became fan favorites during his time in the Washington, D.C. area.<ref>''[[Slam (magazine)|SLAM]]'' (December 2006). "Issue 103, pg. 26".</ref> Arenas played the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions.

Arenas was suspended for most of the [[2009–10 NBA season]] because of handgun violations stemming from an incident on December 24, 2009, and for subsequent actions that appeared to make light of the incident.

In late 2010, Arenas was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]]. After the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Arenas was the first NBA player to be waived under the "[[amnesty clause]]". He signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2011–12 NBA season]], which would be his final season in the league.

==Early life==
Gilbert Arenas was born in [[Tampa, Florida]], to parents Gilbert Arenas Sr and Mary Francis Robinson. His paternal grandfather [[Hipolito Arenas|Hipolito Arenas Sr]]., was a first-generation [[Cuban Americans|Cuban American]] and also an American [[Negro league baseball|Negro League baseball]] player. Arenas was raised in the [[San Fernando Valley]] section of Los Angeles where he played basketball at [[Grant High School (Los Angeles)|Ulysses S. Grant High School]].<ref>{{cite news|date=October 29, 2006|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2006/10/28/AR2006102800830.html|title=The Psychic Scars That Shaped an NBA Star|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=January 16, 2014|first=Mike|last=Wise}}</ref> His number, #25, was [[Retired number|retired]] by the school.<ref>{{cite web|date=November 20, 2001 |url=http://www.socalhoops.com/prep01/1101/gilbert1120.htm |title=Grant thanks its favorite son |author=Vincent Bonsignore |publisher=[[Socal Hoops]] |access-date=January 16, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111010655/http://www.socalhoops.com/prep01/1101/gilbert1120.htm |archive-date=November 11, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Arenas was a late bloomer, taking the final spot on the national ranking as the 99th in the class of 1999. Before beginning his freshman year at the [[University of Arizona]], Arenas attended [[Michael Jordan]]'s basketball camp and was chosen to play on Jordan's team during a game. He impressed Jordan by scoring eight baskets in his first eight possessions. Following the camp, Jordan told coach [[Lute Olson]] that Arenas deserved time on the court.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trivic |first=Filip |date=2020-12-23 |title=Michael Jordan's amazing gesture after Arenas had kids chant "MJ sucks!" |url=https://www.basketballnetwork.net/old-school/michael-jordans-amazing-gesture-after-arenas-had-kids-chant-mj-sucks |access-date=2024-07-22 |website=Basketball Network |language=en}}</ref> [[Rodney Tention]] recruited Arenas to Arizona during a Summer AAU game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-04-13 |title=Lute disciple Rodney Tention back in college hoops |url=https://tucson.com/lute-disciple-rodney-tention-back-in-college-hoops/article_afce7e48-5e6c-11e9-8495-7f1545e0dd0c.html |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=Arizona Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Arenas played basketball at the University of Arizona. He was 17 years old during his freshman season at Arizona, where he played 34 games, starting 31 of them and averaging 15.4 PPG and 4.1 RPG playing both shooting guard and point guard.<ref name="Rivera">{{cite news |last1=Rivera |first1=Steve |title=17-year-old Arenas' star rising fast at UA |work=Southern Arizona Online |date=1999}}</ref> One of his teammates, [[Richard Jefferson]], would later join him in entering the [[2001 NBA draft]].<ref name=Wildcat>{{cite web|last1=Kelley|first1=James|title=NCAA tournament notes: Pac-12 continues to dominate|url=http://www.wildcat.arizona.edu/article/2015/03/ncaa-tournament-notes-pac-12-continues-to-dominate|publisher=[[University of Arizona]]|access-date=July 11, 2015|date=March 21, 2015}}</ref> In 2001, Arenas' sophomore year, he was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pac-12 Conference 2011–12 Men's Basketball Media Guide |page=120 |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |year=2011 |url=http://catalog.e-digitaleditions.com/issue/45931 |access-date=March 18, 2022}}</ref> He helped lead Arizona to the national championship game, where they lost to the Duke Blue Devils, 82–72. Arenas, who was reportedly dealing with a knee injury, struggled in the championship game. He scored 10 points, grabbing 4 rebounds and dishing 4 assists, shooting 4–17 from the field and 0–4 from 3, in what would be his final game with Arizona. Shortly after the tournament, Arenas announced that he was foregoing his last two years at college and would enter the 2001 NBA draft. NBA scouts thought that Arenas, at the time aged only 19, was Arizona's best pro prospect.<ref name=Courier>{{cite news|title=Arenas makes it official|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=894&dat=20010413&id=AI8KAAAAIBAJ&sjid=HU0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=2919,1644807&hl=en|access-date=July 11, 2015|work=[[The Daily Courier (Arizona)|The Daily Courier]]|date=April 13, 2001}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Golden State Warriors (2001–2003)===
After a productive college career, Arenas entered the [[2001 NBA draft]]. Despite strong consideration from many teams in the first round and even lottery teams such as the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Golden State Warriors]],  and [[Sacramento Kings]], Arenas fell to the second round in part due to his effort in interviews despite strong performances in workouts and scrimmages, being selected with the first pick of the second round (31st overall) by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Arenas stated, "I had my 2-day pre-Draft workout with Celtics. Killed the first one, I skipped the 2nd to heal my Achilles so I can tryout with other teams. Celtic's Jim O'Brien put out the rumor that I was immature, didn't take it seriously. Once I was labelled that I was done as a 1st rounder."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-15 |title=Gilbert Arenas blames the Celtics for tanking his draft stock |url=https://fansided.com/2021/09/15/gilbert-arenas-blames-celtics-tanking-draft-stock/ |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=FanSided |language=en-US}}</ref> While slipping through the draft, Arenas contacted [[Rodney Tention]], who was responsible for recruiting him to Arizona to see if he could return to school. Arenas was shocked teammate [[Richard Jefferson]] was selected ahead of him despite Jefferson mocked commonly in the top 10 to the late lottery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-14 |title=Gilbert Arenas Reveals What He Did The Night Before The Final Four Championship Game |url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/gilbert_arenas_reveals_what_he_did_the_night_before_the_final_four_championship_game/s1_16751_37352912 |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=Yardbarker |language=en}}</ref> Arenas would wear the number 0 on his jersey to signify the number of minutes that experts predicted he would play coming as a 17 year old low end prospect from a small high school going to a college powerhouse in Arizona. 

Arenas made his NBA debut on November 4, 2001, vs the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. After not playing his first 3 games, Arenas went scoreless. Arenas scored his first point a free throw in a game vs the [[Toronto Raptors]] on November 7, 2001. Arenas made his first field goal on January 16, 2002, in a game vs the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] scoring 7 points and going 3–4 from the field. Arenas made his first career start on February 15, 2002, and on February 17, 2002, vs the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Arenas had his first double digit scoring game with 12 points; he continued the streak to 9 games with one double double in that stretch. Arenas started 30 games and averaged 10.9 points per game for the Warriors, who finished in last place in the Western Conference that season. Arenas was often forced to sleep at the [[Oracle Arena|Warriors' arena]] due to lavish spending of his rookie money and signing bonus. He later stated the time at the arena allowed him to focus on his game and become a better player.<ref name="NYP">{{cite web |last1=Lemoncelli |first1=Jennifer |title=Gilbert Arenas slept at Oracle Arena after spending Warriors rookie salary |url=https://nypost.com/2021/12/28/gilbert-arenas-slept-at-oracle-arena-after-spending-rookie-salary/ |website=[[New York Post]] |access-date=June 18, 2025 |date=December 28, 2021}}</ref>

In [[2002–03 NBA season|2002–03]], his sophomore season, Arenas received the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] averaging 18.3 points, 6.3 assists and 4.7 rebounds as Golden State improved its victory total to 38, up from 21 last season with Arenas leading the charge, and was named Most Valuable Player of the [[Rising Stars Challenge|Rookie-Sophomore]] game during the [[NBA All-Star Weekend]]. Arenas had a 33 game stretch where he averaged 23.4 PPG, 5.7 APG, and 4.7 RPG with 1.5 SPG on 46.7% FG and 37.7% from 3.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gilbert Arenas 2002-03 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/arenagi01/gamelog/2003/ |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Arenas had one of the best performances of his career during March 2003, when he dropped 41 points, grabbed six rebounds and dished five assists in a win against the Wizards which would be the team that made him their franchise player after the Warriors were unable to match.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-28 |title=A look back at Gilbert Arenas and his career with the Warriors |url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2020/05/28/a-look-back-at-gilbert-arenas-and-his-career-with-the-warriors/ |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=Warriors Wire |language=en-US}}</ref> Arenas said after he won the Most Improved Player award that he didn't think there was much to improve, and he had only needed more playing time and more experience.<ref>{{Cite news |agency=Associated Press |date=2003-05-02 |title=N.B.A.: ROUNDUP; Golden State's Arenas Is Most Improved Player |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/05/02/sports/nba-roundup-golden-state-s-arenas-is-most-improved-player.html |access-date=2024-07-23 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2003–2010)===

====2003–04 season====
After the 2002–03 season, Arenas became a [[restricted free agent]]. He reportedly flipped a coin to decide among several teams seeking to sign him, including the [[Washington Wizards|Wizards]], [[Golden State Warriors|Warriors]], and [[Los Angeles Clippers|Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Football Power Rankings |publisher=TheSportsFanNetwork |url=http://www.dcsportsfan.com/Sports/NBA/default.aspx?ArticleID=764 }}{{dead link|date=January 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The Washington Wizards offered him a six-year, $60 million contract making him the face of the franchise after just turning 21 years old. The Warriors were unable to match this offer because they were over the [[NBA salary cap|salary cap]] and because Arenas was a second-round pick. If Arenas had been drafted in the first round, the salary cap had exceptions that would have allowed the Warriors to match the offer sheet. The "[[Gilbert Arenas Rule]]" was later created to allow teams to re-sign restricted free agents who were not first-round picks.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hu |first=Janny |title=Final looks in store for Warrick, Granger |newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |date=June 23, 2005 |page=D-3 |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/chronicle/archive/2005/06/23/SPG47DDGAC1.DTL |archive-date=February 13, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120213180438/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/chronicle/archive/2005/06/23/SPG47DDGAC1.DTL }}</ref> Arenas battled a strained abdominal muscle injury all season which would cause him to have only to start 52 games in his first year in Washington and constantly sitting on the sidelines dropped his shooting percentage instead of breaking out into the franchise cornerstones in his first year Washington envisioned, Arenas still led the team in PPG and APG.

====2004–05 season====
With Arenas being healthy, he teamed up with former teammate guard [[Larry Hughes]] (22.0 points per game) in [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] to give the Wizards the highest-scoring backcourt duo in the NBA. Arenas was selected for his first [[National Basketball Association All-Star Game|NBA All-Star Game]]. He guided the team to a 45-win season and its first playoff berth since 1997. Arenas led the team in scoring with 25.5 ppg, finishing seventh in the league in that category. He also finished sixth in the league in steals per game in 2004–05 with 2.24 (Hughes led the league with 2.93 steals per game).

[[File:ArenasWizards.jpg|thumb|Arenas during his tenure with the Washington Wizards]] 
In the fifth game of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs in 2005, Arenas hit a 16-foot fadeaway as time expired to give the Wizards a 112–110 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. The Wizards eventually won the series, the franchise's first playoff series victory in more than two decades. In the second round, the Wizards were swept by the Miami Heat, who had been the #1 seed in the Eastern Conference.

====2005–06 season====
In 2006, Wizards fansite Wizznutzz.com jokingly nicknamed him "Agent Zero", a nickname Arenas liked so much that it stuck.<ref name="McKenna 2010"/>

Arenas averaged 29.3 points, which ranked fourth among the scoring leaders, two steals (also fourth), and 6.1 assists per game during the [[2005–06 NBA season]]. However, he was not initially chosen for the 2006 [[National Basketball Association All-Star Game|All-Star Game]]. He was named as a replacement after [[Indiana Pacers]] forward–center [[Jermaine O'Neal]] was injured. He also participated in the [[Three-point Shootout]], where he placed second, after [[Dirk Nowitzki]]. The Washington Wizards finished 42–40 and earned the fifth seed in the Eastern Conference.

During the off-season, Arenas said that he was willing to take a pay cut in order to give the Wizards additional money with which to sign available free agents. He had expressed a desire to win a championship with the Wizards. One of Arenas' most memorable plays was a 40-foot jump shot in Round 1 of the 2006 NBA playoffs in which the Wizards were eliminated by the [[LeBron James]]-led Cleveland Cavaliers in six games.

====2006–07 season====
Arenas himself has noted that he withdrew from the United States national team for the 2006 FIBA World Championship because he felt that assistant coaches [[Mike D'Antoni]] and [[Nate McMillan]] had determined the roster even prior to tryouts.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}} Afterward, he stated that he planned on averaging 50 points against their respective teams (Phoenix Suns and [[Portland Trail Blazers]]). He succeeded at his goal versus powerhouse Phoenix, scoring 54 points, including 21-of-37 from the field, 6-of-12 three-pointers (while reportedly eyeing in the direction of Suns chairman [[Jerry Colangelo]]), in a high-scoring 144–139 Wizards win over the Suns.<ref>{{cite news|place=[[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]], Arizona |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261222021 |title=Arenas sinks 54, Nash drops 42 in high-scoring affair |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |date=December 22, 2006 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728181900/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261222021 |archive-date=July 28, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, on February 11 versus the Blazers, he was held to a lowly nine points, including tying the Wizards' franchise record for three-point futility, going 0-for-8 from behind the arc, in a 94–73 loss versus Portland.<ref>{{cite news|date=February 11, 2007 |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270211027 |title=Arenas held to just nine points in Wizards' loss |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105191054/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270211027 |archive-date=November 5, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In an [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] game versus the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on December 17, 2006, at the [[Staples Center]] in Los Angeles, Arenas scored a career-high 60 points, adding 8 rebounds and 8 assists in helping lead the Wizards over the Lakers, 147–141. Arenas holds the Wizards' franchise record for points scored in a game by an individual, a record he now shares with Bradley Beal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/bradley-beals-ties-franchise-record-60-points-wizards-still-lose-nba-025537525.html|title=Bradley Beals ties franchise record with 60 points, Wizards still lose|website=Yahoo Sports|last=Baer|first=Jack|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=January 7, 2021}}</ref> The previous record of 56 points was held by [[Earl Monroe]], achieved in 1968, which was also an overtime game against the Lakers. Arenas' 16 points in the extra period also set an NBA record for most points in one overtime period, surpassing [[Earl Boykins]]' record by one point.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2006/dec/19/20061219-123754-5995r/?page=all |title=60 |newspaper=[[The Washington Times]] |date=December 19, 2006 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=April 19, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419221944/http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2006/dec/19/20061219-123754-5995r/?page=all }}</ref>

On January 3, 2007, Arenas hit a 32-foot buzzer-beater to win the game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], 108–105.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270103027 |title=Arenas plays with pain, lifts Wiz over Bucks at buzzer |agency=AP |publisher=ESPN |date=January 3, 2007 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140420025611/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270103027 |archive-date=April 20, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Two weeks later on [[Martin Luther King Jr. Day]] he hit another buzzer-beating three-pointer to beat the [[Utah Jazz]], 114–111, in a thriller at the [[Capital One Arena|Verizon Center]].<ref>{{cite news|date=January 15, 2007|title=Arenas (51 points) hits 3 at final horn to drown out Jazz|publisher=ESPN|place=[[Capital One Arena|Verizon Center]], Washington, D.C.|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270115027|url-status=dead|access-date=September 23, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105190942/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270115027|archive-date=November 5, 2012}}</ref> This same scenario has been added as a cut scene in the video game ''[[NBA Live]] 2008''. He also hit a game-winning layup as time expired to beat the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] on March 21, 2007.<ref>{{cite news|agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |date=March 21, 2007 |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270321025 |title=Arenas nets 42, records winner to power Wizards by Sonics |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=November 5, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105190953/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270321025 }}</ref>

[[File:Gilbert Arenas and Eddie Jones.jpg|thumb|right|Arenas (left) in 2007]]
In February 2007, during the final days of All-Star voting, Arenas was voted as a first-time starter for the [[2007 NBA All-Star]] game for the Eastern Conference, edging out [[Vince Carter]] by a slight margin, with 1,454,166 votes to Carter's 1,451,156.<ref name=allstarvote>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2007/news/story?id=2743007 |title=Arenas edges Carter for starting nod; LeBron is top pick |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |date=February 17, 2007 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100929233754/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/allstar2007/news/story?id=2743007 |archive-date=September 29, 2010 |url-status=live }}</ref> At the time he was averaging 29.7 points per game, and led all Eastern Conference point guards in scoring and was second in the league.<ref name=allstarvote/>

Towards the end of the season, Arenas tore his [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] during a game against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], when [[Gerald Wallace]] fell into his leg. The Wizards struggled to finish the season with Arenas and teammate [[Caron Butler]] both being injured. Washington earned a playoff berth, but was swept in the first round in a rematch with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. This was the last season Arenas made an All-Star game and All-NBA team before constant injuries and off-court issues.

====2007–08 season====
During the off-season, Arenas told ''[[The Washington Post]]'' that he would opt out of his contract after the 2007–08 season, making him a free agent. He stated, "if something happens where they don't want me or they're going in a different direction, I can look elsewhere. But my intentions are not to leave."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2899563 |title=Arenas says he'll opt out of deal after 2007–08 season – NBA |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=June 10, 2007 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105191100/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=2899563 |archive-date=November 5, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Arenas only played eight games during the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], due to a knee injury, before he started practicing again in March, and returned to action on April 2, 2008, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]],<ref name=return>{{cite news|publisher=ESPN |date=April 3, 2008 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3326339 |title=Dramatic entrance, reverse layup mark Arenas's return to Wizards |archive-date=December 7, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081207173053/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=3326339 |url-status=live}}</ref> scoring 17 points in a 110–109 home loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280402027 |title=Milwaukee @ Washington recap, April 1, 2008 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |date=April 2, 2008 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017014830/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280402027 |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ten days prior, Arenas stormed out of the locker room before a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280323027 |title=Jamison, Wizards send Pistons to second straight loss |publisher=ESPN |date=March 23, 2008 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105191115/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280323027 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 5, 2012}}</ref> He had wanted to play, but his doctor did not give him clearance.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=ESPN |access-date=September 23, 2010 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3308594 |title=Arenas anxious to play but Wizards won't clear All-Star |date=March 23, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105191120/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=3308594 |url-status=live |archive-date=November 5, 2012}}</ref> Arenas made a surprise return on April 9, when he came out of the locker room with 5:30 left in the first quarter. He finished the game scoring 13 points and dishing out 3 assists in helping the Wizards beat the [[Boston Celtics]], 109–95.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280409027 |title=Jamison's jam on KG helps Wizards take season series with Celts |publisher=ESPN |date=April 9, 2008 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=October 22, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022184256/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280409027}}</ref> He came off the bench for the rest of the regular season as not to disrupt the chemistry the Wizards had built without him. Arenas got his wish when they matched up against the Cavaliers for the third straight year; however, it was apparent he was not 100% healthy. In games 1–3, he played limited minutes, citing soreness in his surgically repaired knee. A few minutes before game 4 of their first-round playoff appearance against the Cavaliers, Arenas announced he would sit out the rest of the playoffs.<ref name=return />

====2008–09 season====
On June 9, 2008, Arenas officially opted out of the final year of his [[contract]], but said that he would re-sign with the Wizards if they retained teammate [[Antawn Jamison]], also a free agent. The Wizards did indeed sign Jamison to a contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/wizards/2008-06-10-arenas_N.htm |title=Wizards' Arenas opts out of final year of contract |date=June 10, 2008 |newspaper=USA Today |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419212654/http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/wizards/2008-06-10-arenas_N.htm |url-status=live |archive-date=April 19, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=Ivan Carter|date=June 10, 2008|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/06/09/AR2008060902435.html|title=It's Official: Arenas Will Test Market|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref> Arenas was offered a five-year contract worth more than $100 million by the [[Golden State Warriors]] and another max deal by the Wizards, a six-year deal worth $124 million.<ref>{{cite news|date=July 2008 |url=http://blog.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2008/07/wiz_offer_arenas_the_max_but_h.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907181329/http://blog.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2008/07/wiz_offer_arenas_the_max_but_h.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 7, 2008 |publisher=Blog.washingtonpost.com |title=Wiz offer Arenas the max but he may take less |last=Carter |first=Ivan |access-date=September 23, 2010 }}</ref> Arenas was teammates with Jamison during their time in Golden State.

On July 13, 2008, Arenas signed a six-year contract worth $111 million with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nba_news/wizards_arenas_080703.html |title=Reports: Arenas Agrees to $111 Million Deal with Wizards |author=Joseph White, AP Sports Writer |date=July 4, 2008 |work=NBA.com |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=April 26, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140426092842/http://www.nba.com/nba_news/wizards_arenas_080703.html }}</ref>

Due to the lingering injuries from [[2006–07 NBA season|April 2007]], Arenas would not make his season debut until March 28, 2009, scoring 15 points and dishing 10 assists in a 98–96 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/detroit-pistons-washington-wizards-2009032827/ |title=Scores, Rumors, Fantasy Games, and more |work=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=April 19, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419212000/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/detroit-pistons-washington-wizards-2009032827/ }}</ref>

He also played a second and final game against the number one seed [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on April 2, in which both teams wore their respective throwback jerseys. Arenas dished out 10 assists and scored 11 points, in a win, and fans were excited to see Arenas, [[Brendan Haywood]], [[Antawn Jamison]], and [[Caron Butler]] re-uniting for the only time in the season. However, the Wizards finished poorly with a record of 19–63, the second-worst record in the NBA, tied with the Los Angeles Clippers, ending four years of consecutive playoff appearances.

====2009–10 season====
Arenas opened the [[2009–2010 NBA season|2009–10 season]] on a hopeful note, scoring 29 points as the Wizards beat the [[Dallas Mavericks]] 102–91 in their season opener. However, Arenas' performance would be inconsistent in the weeks ahead; on November 11, he set a Wizards team record for turnovers in a game with 12.<ref name="thehoopdoctors.com">{{cite web |date=November 11, 2009 |url=http://thehoopdoctors.com/online2/2009/11/gilbert-arenas-sets-franchise-record-for-turnovers/ |title=Gilbert Arenas Sets Franchise Record for Turnovers |publisher=The Hoop Doctors |archive-date=April 20, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140420023755/http://thehoopdoctors.com/online2/2009/11/gilbert-arenas-sets-franchise-record-for-turnovers/ |access-date=January 8, 2010 }}</ref> On December 12, Arenas netted his first [[triple-double]] in {{frac|5|1|2}} years in a loss to the Pacers.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/pacers_edge_wizards_despite_arenas_triple_double/1736222 |title=Pacers edge Wizards despite Arenas's triple-double |agency=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 12, 2009 |publisher=[[Yardbarker]] |archive-date=November 29, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129023138/http://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/pacers_edge_wizards_despite_arenas_triple_double/1736222 }}</ref> Six days later Arenas had a season-best 45 points in a Wizards win over his former team, the Golden State Warriors.

====Firearms incident====
On December 24, 2009, it was reported that Arenas had admitted to storing unloaded firearms in his locker at the [[Capital One Arena|Verizon Center]] and had surrendered them to team security. In doing so, Arenas not only violated NBA rules against bringing firearms into an arena, but also violated D.C. ordinances as well.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4771109 |title=Report: NBA investigating Wizards guard Gilbert Arenas for gun possession |date=December 25, 2009 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100924142553/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=4771109 |archive-date=September 24, 2010 |url-status=live }}</ref> On January 1, 2010, it was also reported that Arenas and teammate [[Javaris Crittenton]] had drawn guns on each other in the Wizards' locker room during a Christmas Eve argument regarding gambling debts. The [[D.C. Metropolitan Police]] and the [[United States Attorney for the District of Columbia|U.S. Attorney]]'s office began investigating,<ref>{{cite news|work=[[Fox News]] |title=NBA Players Reportedly Drew Guns in Christmas Eve Argument |date=January 1, 2010 |url=https://www.foxnews.com/us/nba-players-reportedly-drew-guns-in-christmas-eve-argument/ |archive-date=April 20, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140420031705/http://www.foxnews.com/us/2010/01/01/nba-players-reportedly-drew-guns-christmas-eve-argument/ }}</ref> and on January 14, 2010, Arenas was charged with carrying a pistol without a license, a violation of Washington, D.C.'s gun-control laws.<ref>{{cite news|title=Wizards' Arenas Is Charged With Felony |date=January 14, 2010 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/01/15/sports/basketball/15arenas.html |author=Howard Beck |newspaper=The New York Times |access-date=January 14, 2010 |archive-date=January 28, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100128053351/http://www.nytimes.com/2010/01/15/sports/basketball/15arenas.html }}</ref> Arenas pleaded guilty on January 15 to the felony of carrying an unlicensed pistol outside a home or business.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/michael_mccann/01/25/crittenton.wizards/index.html?cnn=yes&hpt=T2 |title=Crittenton's plea agreement on gun charges could affect Arenas's future |date=January 25, 2010 |agency=[[CNN]] |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 3, 2010 |archive-date=June 4, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604015339/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/michael_mccann/01/25/crittenton.wizards/index.html?cnn=yes&hpt=T2 }}</ref>

On January 6, 2010, Arenas' 28th birthday, the NBA suspended him indefinitely without pay until its investigation was complete. By nearly all accounts, the league felt compelled to act when Arenas' teammates surrounded him during pregame introductions prior to a game with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and he pretended to shoot them with guns made from his fingers. [[NBA Commissioner]] [[David Stern]] said in a statement that Arenas' behavior after the investigation started "has led me to conclude that he is not currently fit to take the court in an NBA game." He also said that Arenas was likely facing a lengthy suspension.<ref>{{cite news |author=J.E. Skeets |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/blog/ball_dont_lie/post/Gilbert-Arenas-continues-to-take-gun-case-in-str?urn=nba,212006 |title=Gilbert Arenas continues to take gun case in stride |date=September 15, 2010 |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=January 9, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100109211926/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/blog/ball_dont_lie/post/Gilbert-Arenas-continues-to-take-gun-case-in-str?urn=nba%2C212006 }}</ref> The Wizards issued a statement of their own condemning the players' pregame stunt as "unacceptable".<ref>{{cite news|website=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4802267 |title=Washington Wizards' |date=March 23, 2010 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4862783 |title=Stern bans Arenas, Crittenton for year |author=Marc Stein and Chris Sheridan |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=December 2, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101202213527/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=4862783 }}</ref> On February 2, 2010, Arenas wrote an open [[editorial]] in ''[[The Washington Post]]'', in which he apologized for his actions, particularly for failing to be a better [[role model]] to young fans and for "making light of a serious situation."<ref>{{cite news|date=February 2, 2010|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/02/01/AR2010020102795.html|title=Gilbert Arenas: Learning to be a better role After the first 24 games of the season, Arenas led the Wizards with an average of 17.3 points per game but the team had one of the worst win-loss records in the league at 6–18.

===Orlando Magic (2010–2011)===
[[File:ArenasOrlando.jpg|thumb|Arenas with the Magic in 2010]]
On December 18, 2010, Arenas was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] for [[Rashard Lewis]].<ref>{{cite news|website=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/news_arenas_121810.html|title=Magic Acquire Gilbert Arenas From Wizards|date=December 18, 2010|access-date=December 18, 2010}}</ref> Arenas was reunited with former Warriors teammate and draftmate [[Jason Richardson]] in Orlando. Arenas chose to wear #1 on his jersey in honor of his favorite player, [[Penny Hardaway]]. He was the backup point guard, with [[Jameer Nelson]] at the starting role.<ref>{{cite web|work=[[CBS Sports]] |url=http://www.cbssports.com/mcc/blogs/entry/22748484/26563802 |title=Gilbert Arenas will wear No.1 for Penny Hardaway |date=December 20, 2010 |access-date=December 20, 2010 |archive-date=March 10, 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310145003/http://www.cbssports.com/mcc/blogs/entry/22748484/26563802 }}</ref> The Magic finished 52–30 and clinched the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference and made the playoffs. However, Orlando lost to the Atlanta Hawks in six games in the opening round of the playoffs.

On December 9, 2011, after the end of the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Arenas was waived by the Orlando Magic under the [[NBA salary cap#amnesty|amnesty clause]], being the first player to be waived under the newly established clause at the time of its inclusion.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news_arenas_120911.html |title=Magic Waive Arenas Via Amnesty |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=December 9, 2011 |access-date=December 9, 2011 |archive-date=January 7, 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107225229/http://www.nba.com/magic/news_arenas_120911.html }}</ref> He cleared waivers and became a free agent. Due to the 2011 NBA lockout, the 2011–12 NBA season was reduced from its normal 82 games to 66 games.<ref>{{cite news|author=Marc Stein |date=December 11, 2011 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7342625/gilbert-arenas-now-unrestricted-free-agent-clearing-waivers-sources-say |title=Gilbert Arenas now an unrestricted free agent after clearing waivers, sources say |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 16, 2013 |archive-date=January 2, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130102061336/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/7342625/gilbert-arenas-now-unrestricted-free-agent-clearing-waivers-sources-say }}</ref>

In the summer of 2011, Arenas acted with former Wizards teammate [[Etan Thomas]] in a dramatic production of ''[[Our Town]]'' by [[Thornton Wilder]].

===Memphis Grizzlies (2012)===
On March 20, 2012, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] signed Arenas. His primary role was again a backup point guard, this time to [[Mike Conley Jr.]] The Grizzlies finished 41–25 and clinched the fourth seed in the Western Conference. However, they lost in the first round to the Los Angeles Clippers in a full seven-game series.<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/story/2012-03-20/Gilbert-Arenas-signs-with-Grizzlies/53670596/1|title=Gilbert Arenas signs pro-rated deal with Grizzlies|work=[[USA Today]]|date=March 20, 2012|access-date=March 20, 2012}}</ref> Arenas' final NBA game was played in seventh and deciding game of the 2012 Western Conference First Round on May 13, 2012. Memphis lost to the Los Angeles Clippers, with Arenas only playing for 3 minutes and recording no stats; Arenas was only 30 years old in his final NBA game.

===Shanghai Sharks (2012–2013)===
On November 19, 2012, Arenas signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). In his one season in the CBA, Arenas averaged 20.7 points per game, 7.3 rebounds per game, and 3.0 assists per game in 27.3 minutes per game. He played in 14 games and started in 8 of them. However, the Sharks finished at 10–22 and missed the playoffs.<ref>{{cite news|access-date=November 20, 2012|newspaper=[[Bangkok Post]]|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/news/sports/322058/nba-star-gilbert-arenas-joins-shanghai-sharks|title=NBA star Gilbert Arenas joins Shanghai Sharks|date=November 19, 2012}}</ref>

==Personal life==

One of Arenas' cousins is [[Javier Arenas (American football)|Javier Arenas]], a professional football player who played for the [[NFL]]'s [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Select CB Javier Arenas with second Pick in Round 2|url=http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Select-CB-Javier-Arenas-with-second-Pick-in-Round-2/d7445c81-1781-4498-a0cb-9c2ad64e0903|work=KCChiefs.com|access-date=November 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140319000127/http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Select-CB-Javier-Arenas-with-second-Pick-in-Round-2/d7445c81-1781-4498-a0cb-9c2ad64e0903|archive-date=March 19, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Another cousin, Armando Murillo, has played in the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cflstats.ca/player/7167/armando-murillo|title=Armando Murillo {{!}} CFL Football Statistics {{!}} CflStats.ca|website=cflstats.ca|access-date=January 31, 2017|archive-date=January 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190106153417/http://cflstats.ca/player/7167/armando-murillo|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Arenas is a friend of rapper [[The Game (rapper)|the Game]] and was listed in the booklet for the Game's second album ''[[Doctor's Advocate]]''. 

He collects a synthetic basketball from each team played, as well as players' jerseys, of which he has more than 400, most of which are autographed.<ref name="esquire">{{cite news|title=The Pathology of Gilbert Arenas |first=Tom |last=Chiarella |date=January 6, 2010 |access-date=February 18, 2007 |url=http://www.esquire.com/features/sports/ESQ1106gilbert |work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515020013/http://www.esquire.com/features/sports/ESQ1106gilbert |archive-date=May 15, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> He supported [[People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals|PETA]]'s anti-fur mission by posing shirtless for their Ink, Not Mink campaign.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.aolnews.com/2010/03/03/gilbert-arenas-shrugs-off-sentencing-nerves/ |author=Joseph White |title=Gilbert Arenas Works with PETA While Awaiting Sentence |publisher=[[AOL|AOL News]] |date=March 3, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114023854/http://www.aolnews.com/2010/03/03/gilbert-arenas-shrugs-off-sentencing-nerves/ |archive-date=November 14, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Arenas donated $100 for every point he scored in each home game during the 2006–07 season to local D.C.-area schools, while Wizards team owner [[Abe Pollin]] matched that contribution for each away game.<ref>{{Cite news|title=82 Schools Win the Lottery, Wizards-Style|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/10/29/AR2007102901892.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=October 30, 2007|access-date=November 29, 2015|issn=0190-8286|language=en-US|first=Darragh|last=Johnson}}</ref> He has also mentored a D.C. boy who lost his family in a fire at age 10. Arenas got him a job as a ball boy for the Wizards.<ref name="wapo-gilbertology">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A12185-2005Apr23.html|title=Wizards Learn to Love 'Gilbertology'|first=Michael|last=Lee |newspaper=The Washington Post|date=April 24, 2005|page=A1}}</ref>

Arenas has had his own shoe, the [[Adidas]] Gil Zero, as well as his own line of Adidas TS Lightswitch shoes. Arenas wears size 14{{frac|1|2}} shoes.<ref name="shoe_size-gilbertology">{{cite web |url=http://www.gilbertology.net/gilbertology-from-gilbert-arenas/ |title=Gilbertology by Gilbert Arenas |website=Gilbertology.net |access-date=September 23, 2010 |archive-date=August 31, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130831103716/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1751242-gilbert-arenas-shares-how-he-avoids-traffic-tickets-and-more-driving-advice}}</ref> Following the gun incident in 2009, Adidas dropped their sponsorship of Arenas. Instead of signing another endorsement deal, he turned to his vast collection of shoes. For nearly every game of the season, Arenas wore a different pair of shoes,<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bierman|first1=Fred|title=Gilbert Arenas's $395 High Tops|url=https://offthedribble.blogs.nytimes.com/2010/12/11/gilbert-arenass-395-high-tops/|access-date=March 2, 2018|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=December 11, 2010}}</ref> wearing a total of 77 different pairs.{{citation needed|date=July 2015}}

Arenas admitted that he ran about 60 red lights in 4 months and got away with it by keeping his dealer plates on his vehicle.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1751242-gilbert-arenas-shares-how-he-avoids-traffic-tickets-and-more-driving-advice |title=Gilbert Arenas Shares How He Avoids Traffic Tickets and More Driving Advice |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=August 26, 2013 |author=Tristan Thornburgh |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130831103716/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1751242-gilbert-arenas-shares-how-he-avoids-traffic-tickets-and-more-driving-advice |archive-date=August 31, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
